commands.pickDate_comment: Command palette entry. Opens the picker for the date at the cursor.

notes.notes_comment: Heading of the settings section covering how a date behaves in a note: what opens the calendar, and what is drawn around a date under the pointer.
notes.heading: Dates in a note

commandOnly.name_comment: Small line at the top of the 'Dates in a note' section, shown only when both the double-click and the hover icon are switched off, so nothing in a note opens the calendar any more. {{command}} is replaced by the name of the Pick a date command, taken from commands.pickDate so it matches the command palette whatever the command is called — keep the marker, and quote it with your language's quotation marks. Keep 'Note:', or your language's equivalent, as an opener. For 'command palette', use the words your language's Obsidian uses for it. The reader chose this, so word it as a fact, not a warning.
commandOnly.name: Note: Only “{{command}}” from the command palette opens the calendar

calendar.calendar_comment: Heading of the settings section covering what the calendar itself shows once open.
calendar.heading: Calendar

doubleClick.name_comment: Settings row label for the toggle that lets a double-click on a date open the calendar.
doubleClick.name: Double-click
doubleClick.desc: Double-click a date to open the calendar.

hoverIcon.name_comment: Settings row label for the dropdown controlling the small icon that appears beside a date while the pointer is over it.
hoverIcon.name: Icon on hover
hoverIcon.desc_comment: Description under that dropdown. {{icon}} is replaced by the icon itself, drawn inline — keep the marker, and put it where the icon reads naturally in your language.
hoverIcon.desc: Click the {{icon}} that appears when the pointer is over a date.

options.off_comment: Dropdown option: no icon appears at all.
options.left_comment: Dropdown option: the icon appears before the date.
options.right_comment: Dropdown option: the icon appears after the date. The default.

hoverFrame.name_comment: Settings row label for the toggle that draws an outline around a date and its icon while the pointer is over them.
hoverFrame.name: Outline on hover

weekNumbers.name_comment: Settings row label for the toggle adding a week-number column to the calendar. Off by default.
weekNumbers.name: Week numbers

weekStart.name_comment: Settings row label for the dropdown choosing which day a week starts on in the calendar.
weekStart.name: First day of the week

writesPreview.name_comment: Settings row label for the toggle showing, in the calendar, the exact text a pick will write into the note.
writesPreview.name: Preview the new date

formats.heading_comment: Heading above the list of date formats the plugin looks for.
formats.heading: Date formats
formats.description_comment: The single line of explanation under the Date formats heading. 'Applied top to bottom' means that when two formats could both read the same text, the one higher in the list wins.
formats.description: The date formats Kalendae recognises in your notes, applied top to bottom.
formats.add_comment: Tooltip on the + button beside the Date formats heading, which opens a menu of formats to add.
formats.addCustom_comment: Last entry in the add menu, below the built-in formats. Opens a page for writing a format of your own.
formats.builtIn_comment: Hover label on the icon at the start of a format row that came with Kalendae. These formats cannot be edited, only removed or reordered.
formats.custom_comment: Hover label on the icon at the start of a format row the user wrote themselves. Contrasts with the built-in formats; these are the only ones with an edit button.
formats.newFormat_comment: Row label for a custom format that has been added but not yet given a pattern.
formats.unfinished_comment: Shown in place of the example on a format row whose pattern is incomplete or uses tokens Kalendae cannot read.
formats.edit_comment: Accessible label on the pencil button of a custom format row.
formats.delete_comment: Accessible label on the delete button of a format row.
formats.reorder_comment: Accessible label on the drag handle at the start of a format row.
formats.shadow_comment: Hover labels on the icon of a format row that an earlier format in the list beats to its dates. {{by}} is that earlier format's pattern, not translated. Three cases with three different answers: move the row up, remove one of the pair, or nothing at all.

shadow.move: Never used: {{by}} above it claims these dates first. Move this above it.
shadow.remove: Never used: {{by}} above it reads the same dates. Remove one.
shadow.shared: Shares dates with {{by}}. Where both fit, the one above wins.

modal.title_comment: Title of the dialog for writing or editing a custom date format.
modal.title: Custom format
modal.pattern_comment: Label for the text field holding the format pattern.
modal.required_comment: Shown after the name of a part a format cannot do without — year, month and day. Keep the brackets if they read naturally in your language.
modal.optional_comment: Shown after the name of a part a format may leave out, currently only the day of the week.
modal.columns_comment: Headings of the three columns in the token table: the tokens themselves, what each one writes, and whether the format being edited uses one.

groups.year_comment: Checklist row in the custom format dialog. The tokens beside it (YY, YYYY) are not translated. A tick appears when the format includes one of them.
groups.month_comment: Checklist row for the month tokens M, MM, MMM, MMMM.
groups.day_comment: Checklist row for the day-of-month tokens D, DD, Do.
groups.weekday_comment: Row for the weekday tokens d, dd, ddd, dddd. The only optional part, and the only row with no tick or cross beside it — there is nothing to satisfy.
groups.literal_comment: Last row of the token table, describing the punctuation between tokens rather than a part of a date. Everything that is not a letter is written into the note exactly as typed, so this row has no tick.

modal.warning_comment: Shown when a format holds nothing but numbers, as in YYYYMMDD, so a plain number in a note would match it. {{digits}} is how many digits it matches. A format with anything else in it — a separator, a month name — never shows this. Not an error, the format saves, so it is worded as advice.
modal.warning: Your format matches any {{digits}}-digit number. Consider adding separators.
modal.hint_comment: Shown where the error message goes while the format field is still empty. Not an error — nothing is wrong yet — so it is worded as a next step and shown in ordinary text rather than the error colour.
modal.hint: Write a format using the tokens above.

problem.adjacent_comment: Shown when a one-or-two-digit token touches another number and neither can be given a fixed width. {{first}} and {{second}} are the two tokens, not translated. Such a format cannot be read back reliably, so it cannot be saved.
problem.adjacent: Your format is ambiguous: {{first}} and {{second}} run together. Add a separator.
problem.adjacentWiden_comment: The same problem where one of the two tokens has a fixed-width form, as YYMDD does: {{from}} is M or D and {{to}} is MM or DD. Two ways out, and widening the token keeps the format's shape.
problem.adjacentWiden: Your format is ambiguous: {{first}} and {{second}} run together. Add a separator, or write {{from}} as {{to}}.
problem.adjacentWidenBoth_comment: The same problem where both tokens have a fixed-width form, as MDYYYY does. {{firstFixed}} and {{secondFixed}} are the widened tokens, in the same order as {{first}} and {{second}}.
problem.adjacentWidenBoth: Your format is ambiguous: {{first}} and {{second}} run together. Add a separator, or write them as {{firstFixed}} and {{secondFixed}}.

missing.year_comment: Shown beside the buttons when the format has no year. The tokens are not translated.
missing.year: A format needs a year: add YY or YYYY.
missing.month_comment: Shown beside the buttons when the format has no month. The tokens are not translated.
missing.month: A format needs a month: add M, MM, MMM or MMMM.
missing.day_comment: Shown beside the buttons when the format has no day of the month. The tokens are not translated.
missing.day: A format needs a day: add D, DD or Do.

problem.unknownTokens_comment: Shown beside the buttons when the format contains letters Kalendae has no token for. {{chars}} is those letters as typed, and may be more than one run of them separated by commas.
problem.brackets_comment: Shown beside the buttons when the format holds a pair of square brackets. The date library reads anything between [ and ] as text to reproduce rather than as tokens, so such a format can never match a date and cannot be saved. Keep the [ and ] characters as they are and translate only the words around them. A bracket with no partner is fine and does not show this.

modal.cancel_comment: Button that closes the custom format dialog without keeping the format.
modal.save_comment: Button that keeps the custom format and closes the dialog. Unavailable while a required part is missing.

scopes.heading_comment: Label of the row that opens the page controlling which parts of a note are searched, and the title of that page.
scopes.heading: Sections to scan

text.name_comment: The first section on the Sections to scan page: the prose body of a note, as opposed to its headings, frontmatter, code or links. Always scanned, shown with a toggle that is on and cannot be moved.
text.name: Body text

headings.name_comment: Toggle label: markdown headings, the lines starting with #. On by default, unlike the other optional sections.
headings.name: Headings

frontmatter.name_comment: Toggle label: the YAML properties block at the top of a note.
frontmatter.name: Frontmatter

inlineCode.name_comment: Toggle label: short code spans written between single backticks.
inlineCode.name: Inline code

codeBlocks.name_comment: Toggle label: fenced code blocks written between triple backticks.
codeBlocks.name: Code blocks

wikilinks.name_comment: Toggle label: Obsidian's internal links, written between double square brackets.
wikilinks.name: Wikilinks

sample.heading_comment: Heading above the worked example at the bottom of the Sections to scan page.
sample.heading: Preview
sample.description_comment: Explains the example block on the Sections to scan page. Must make clear that the plugin never highlights dates in the user's own notes at all — not that it highlights them differently.
sample.description: An example note, shown for demonstration only. Kalendae does not highlight dates in your notes.
sample.detected_comment: Legend label for the colour marking dates the plugin would pick up.
sample.skipped_comment: Legend label for the colour marking dates the plugin would leave alone because their section is switched off.

picker.today_comment: Button under the calendar that sets the date to today and closes the picker. The only shortcut the picker ships with.
picker.weekColumn_comment: Heading of the optional week-number column, at the left edge of the calendar. Kept to two or three characters: the column is one number wide.
picker.prevMonth_comment: Screen-reader label for the single left chevron above the calendar. The button shows no text.
picker.nextMonth_comment: Screen-reader label for the single right chevron above the calendar.
picker.prevYear_comment: Screen-reader label for the double left chevron above the calendar, which steps a whole year.
picker.nextYear_comment: Screen-reader label for the double right chevron above the calendar.

notices.noEditor_comment: Notice shown when the Pick a date command runs somewhere there is no editor to read.
notices.noEditor: Open a note in editing view first.
notices.noDateHere_comment: Notice shown when the Pick a date command runs somewhere with no recognised date at or beside the cursor.
notices.noDateHere: No date here. Put the cursor on a date first.
